title: Guild Acoustic
description: Several years ago I was browsing around a small music store when a man entered with a guitar case. He made his way to the counter and started talking to the clerk. I was trying out some old mandolins. I could hear that the man was looking to trade in his acoustic guitar for an electric. Time passed and I continued onto a dusty old electric piano. The man who had entered the store was done making his deal and walked out with a brand new electric guitar. As I turned around, the clerk behind the counter was standing on a ladder hoisting his newly acquired acoustic guitar high up onto a hook on the wall. He had barely started to come down the ladder when I said "How much for the that thing?".  I play this guitar every single day. I take it with me on long weekends up north. I've burned countless hours mindlessly strumming chords and picking tunes on it. I love this guitar.

description: www.ardentoctopus.podshow.com From the 60's, paid $100.00 around 1987 it has a bridge pickup that got fried many years ago. title: 2003 Faith Saturn electro-acoustic guitar
description: In 2003 I was looking for a "proper" acoustic guitar, as my next step up from the Washburn D10 I'd played for ages. A Martin D28 or (drool) D35 being somewhat out of my price bracket, I was about to choose a Simon and Patrick, Seagull or Norman (i.e. a mid-range Canadian guitar) when I discovered the Faith brand. Made by a family-run factory in Indonesia, I tried the Faith Saturn (their 'dreadnought' model) and was instantly smitten.  It records beautifully with a condenser mike in front of it, and although I haven't used the pre-amp output much (as I don't play 'live' with it very often), it's handy to have... and unlike any other electro-acoustic in its range that I've ever seen, it has an XLR output.

title: ModelsOverview
description: I’ve been building guitars for three and a half decades, and even though my factory has grown large, I’ve personally made thousands of guitars. One at a time. There is something so gripping about painstakingly making a guitar—a single guitar—and putting attention into every detail, sandpaper and chisel in hand. A luthier never tires of this.    With the resources of Taylor Guitars at my fingertips, I decided to start a new company that makes guitars in this fashion. One by one, with no detail too small. The quantity, almost by definition, is small because the talent needed to make guitars in this way is very rare and needs to be fostered in a small shop environment.

title: Cocobolo Harvest
tags: 000|hand made|luthier|Russell Guitars|Schoenberg Guitars|Martin|Cocobolo|steel string|acoustic|custom guitars|this just made flickr explore
description: This "000" Schoenberg made by luthier James Russell seems to be growing out of the earth. The back and sides of this 000 are made of Cocobolo Rosewood and the guitar has Ebony binding. Post Script: I had the good fortune to be able to play this guitar again about two years after it was built by my husband James Russell. (It had been sold from the Schoenberg Guitars shop in Tiburon, California.) As I started to play it, I could not believe the sound coming from it. I barely touched the strings and the tones rang and resonated with such fullness and clarity, surrounding me and filling the room. At this moment I decided I was going to make a "000" for myself. I had been trying to figure out exactly what I wanted, and it was this guitar that decided for me. For this reason, this guitar will always be a very special guitar to me. Acoustic guitars do warm, mellow, and develop their voices for many years after being built, but this is beyond what we expected to hear after only two years. It had wonderful sound when it was new, but this was amazing. I have an ongoing set of photos of the building of my 000 guitar here: Apple Crisp Builds Her 000 Guitar. Since my 000 model is a Russell and not a Schoenberg, there are differences between the two models, but there are basic similarities too.

description: The Taylor T5S is a seriously cool guitar, really made for the player who craves variety but doesn't want to truck around 5 guitar cases. You've got a versatility of sounds at your fingertips that will blow you away - mellow acoustic, Les Paul rock crunch, jazz tones, you can do it all with this one guitar. Seriously. The T5S has hidden neck humbucker, a visible bridge humbucker, and a body sensor mounted to the inside surface of the top, utilizing Samarium Cobalt magnets and humbucking coils. The body sensor reads the movement of the top, adding even more warmth to the acoustic tone. And if you want to fatten it up and rock out, or play some 335-inspired rockabilly, or jazz it up, the T5 can take you there and beyond with ease. title: Tom Anderson Crowdster Plus (2758-2)
description: This Tom Anderson Crowdster Plus has a tremendous Burnished Orange flamed Maple top. The body is Mahogany, the neck is Mahogany with an Indian Rosewood fingerboard, satin back with a 1.73 inch nut and small frets. Of course, Buzz Feiten tuning system, LR Baggs CMA and hard case included. See what our own John Flynn has to say about this innovative guitar: I've been playing an Anderson Crowdster Plus for several years and I'm convinced that it's one of the finest instruments ever created. As a worship leader at a church in a very artistic community, we're fortunate enough to be able to reinterpret music from all generations as well as write our own material. This demands a guitar that is not only extremely versatile, but one that allows for unique sounds as well. I feel the Crowdster Plus is the ultimate instrument for this challenge. Sure, it can do the Electric/Acoustic thing better than any other, but I feel its strengths lie in its ability to create many different electric sounds ranging from a pop, rhythmic jangle to a full-on rock drive, but all with its own sweet touch. My favorite is to combine the two pickups and blend in just a hint of the acoustic pickup. By using this setting, it can be extremely delicate but kick on your favorite boost pedal and it creates a great drive tone that's not just another 'heard that a million times' guitar tone. -John Retail is $4139. description: The Taylor T5S is a seriously cool guitar, really made for the player who craves variety but doesn't want to truck around 5 guitar cases. You've got a versatility of sounds at your fingertips that will blow you away - mellow acoustic, Les Paul rock crunch, jazz tones, you can do it all with this one guitar. Seriously. The T5S has hidden neck humbucker, a visible bridge humbucker, and a body sensor mounted to the inside surface of the top, utilizing Samarium Cobalt magnets and humbucking coils. The body sensor reads the movement of the top, adding even more warmth to the acoustic tone. And if you want to fatten it up and rock out, or play some 335-inspired rockabilly, or jazz it up, the T5 can take you there and beyond with ease. The Taylor T5S is beautifully crafted, truly innovative, and a joy to play. Taylor T5 S on www.massstreetmusic.com
